entries.title: II Chronicles 14:1
segments:
CHAP. XIV. 
 
  The piety of Asa, ver. 1-5.   His policy, ver. 6-8.   His victory over the Ethiopians, ver. 9-15. 
 
  V. 1. Quiet-There was no open war, but there were private hostilities between his and Baasha's subjects.

entries.title: II Chronicles 14:6
segments: V. 6. The land had rest-Those have rest indeed, to whom God gives rest; peace indeed, to whom Christ gives peace.  We find by experience, it is good to seek the Lord.  While we pursue the world, we meet with nothing but vexation.

entries.title: II Chronicles 14:9
segments: V. 9. Ethiopian-Or, the Arabian, as the Hebrew word Cush is commonly used: these being much nearer to Asa than the Ethiopians.

entries.title: II Chronicles 14:11
segments: V. 11. Let not man prevail-If he prevails against us, he prevails, as it were, against thee; because thou art our God.  And we rest on thee, and go forth in thy name, which thou hast encouraged us to do.

entries.title: II Chronicles 14:12
segments: V. 12. Smote-With terror, and an unaccountable consternation.

entries.title: II Chronicles 14:14
segments: V. 14. Smote the cities-because they had joined, with Zerah in this war.
